appraisal_events.evidence: se redressant avec le dépit d'une grande coquette trahie, il répondit: « Je vois que vous avez un cœur d'artichaut. » ... M. de Charlus... adressa à Jupien... une prière... et, se décidant à accorder à M. de Charlus ce que celui-ci venait de lui demander, Jupien... dit au baron d'un air souriant, ému, supérieur et reconnaissant: « Oui, va, grand gosse! »
appraisal_events.explanation: Jupien takes real offense at Charlus's wandering attention and rebukes him like a betrayed coquette, forcing the baron to plead and flatter him to smooth things over; Jupien ends the exchange visibly the emotionally superior party, granting his favor from a position of strength.

appraisal_events.evidence: M. de Charlus se servait, avec le giletier, du même langage qu'il eût fait avec des gens du monde de sa coterie... Je descendis aux Aubrais en même temps que ma jeune personne qu'hélas, sa famille... attendait sur le quai! ... « Évêque! s'écria Jupien qui n'avait rien compris des dernières phrases que venait de prononcer M. de Charlus... » ... Il n'a aucunement la notion du prodigieux personnage que je suis et du microscopique vibrion qu'il figure.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus's grandiloquent, class-bound rhetoric -- his absurd tram pursuit ending in failure, his boasts of noble and ecclesiastical lineage, his outrage at a young bourgeois's indifference -- lands on a baffled Jupien and reads as comically incongruous, exposing vanity and obsessive erotic pursuit beneath his self-image as a prodigious personage.

status_effects.explanation: Jupien's rebuke forces Charlus into an appeasing, pleading posture, and Jupien closes the exchange visibly superior and flattered rather than deferential.
Charlus must court Jupien's forgiveness through a murmured plea, temporarily ceding emotional ground despite his aristocratic standing.
Charlus's grandiose self-regard and compulsive erotic anecdotes are framed by the narrator as absurd and out of touch, particularly when they fall flat on an uncomprehending Jupien.

ambiguities: The passage's long closing essay on the nature of inverts as a persecuted 'race' is narratorial reflection rather than a locally witnessed appraisal event about a named character, so it is not scored as a separate event.
